title: BOX OF GARNITURE EWERS (AS IS)...
reason: Pair of gilt and blue ivory ewers in a Worcester style that could be $150 to $400 if English and marked; AS IS suggests damage, so check bases and handles.
findings: Pair of Victorian style garniture ewers: ivory body, pale blue neck, fluted shoulder and square plinth foot, raised gilt bird and bramble (blackberry) decoration, gilt scroll handles with snake-like terminals. The style is consistent with Royal Worcester or Hadleys Worcester c.1880s or a Continental imitation, but no mark is visible (bases not shown), so the maker is unconfirmed. Also in the box: Galileo thermometer, oak aneroid barometer with thermometer, petit-point dial desk clock in a gilt brass arched frame (maker not legible), oval tray with beaded rim (tarnished plate, no hallmark seen), turned wooden urn, blue and white transfer bowl, black-letter souvenir lustre jug (text not legible), sponge-rim jug with a pig vignette and a small floral jug.
condition: Title says AS IS, so faults are expected but none is clearly visible: gilding is rubbed on both plinth edges and the ivory glaze looks speckled and stained; the tray is tarnished and dented; clock glass appears intact.
rescore_note: Pair of ivory and pale blue ewers with raised gilt bird and bramble is the draw, but a Worcester family maker is only a minority chance (no mark seen, stained glaze, AS IS), so the realistic mix sits at the top of the $80 to $200 band, with modest filler items. General knowledge, no web check.
